newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower, tension fear lingers.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower, tension fear lingers.

text.p: Across-the-board consolidation combined with worries about rising inter-Korean tension pushed the Seoul stock market to close lower in Monday's thin trading, brokers said.
The shooting of prominent defector Li Il-nam, a nephew of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il's ex-wife, by suspected North Korean agents triggered fears of growing tension on the Korean peninsula.
The composite stock index shed 9.39 points, or 1.30 percent, to provisionally close at a day low of 712.93. Losers led gainers by 521 to 285.
"The market is in a short-term consolidation. The rising country risk also chilled buying interest," said Hong Jong-hyun of Coryo Securities.

The attack appeared to be a warning to Seoul and potential asylum seekers after high-ranking Pyongyang official Hwang Jang-yop sought political asylum in South Korea. Hwang, ranked 24th in the Stalinist state's hierachy, is now stranded in the South Korean emabassy in Beijing.
"But the shooting and the defector issues will not live long in the market as we experienced in the past cases of North-South Korea confrontation," said Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities.
"Investors saw there was strong resistences around the 720 level. I expect a tug-of-war surrounding that mark," said a Samsung Securities broker.
Brokers said blue chips spearheaded the index fall.
Samsung Electronics shed 2,500 won to 56,000. Steelmaker POSCO fell 900 won to 42,700 and electricity-monopoly KEPCO lost 300 won to 27,600.
Brokers said the signing of the global telecommunications market liberalising pact had no direct impact on the local market on Monday. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
